title: Wastewater permit limits and monitoring practice questions
description: Free NPDES permit limits and monitoring practice questions on 40 CFR 122.42–122.50. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.topic: Additional conditions for specified permit categories
questions.question: Under 122.42(b), who must give the Director adequate notice of any new introduction of pollutants from an indirect discharger that would be subject to section 301 or 306 of the CWA if it were discharging directly?

options.A: The indirect discharger alone
options.B: All POTWs
options.C: The EPA Regional Administrator
options.D: The State water quality standards agency

questions.explanation: "All POTWs must provide adequate notice to the Director of the following: (1) Any new introduction of pollutants into the POTW from an indirect discharger which would be subject to section 301 or 306 of CWA if it were directly discharging those pollutants"

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.42, Additional conditions applicable to specified categories of NPDES permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: All POTWs must provide adequate notice to the Director of the following: (1) Any new introduction of pollutants into the POTW from an indirect discharger which would be subject to section 301 or 306 of CWA if it were directly discharging those pollutants

questions.topic: Additional conditions for specified permit categories
questions.question: What does 122.42(b)(3) say adequate notice from a POTW shall include?

options.A: The name of each industrial user's certified operator
options.B: A copy of each indirect discharger's production records
options.C: Results of a whole effluent toxicity test on the POTW's sludge
options.D: Information on the quality and quantity of effluent introduced into the POTW, and any anticipated impact of the change on the quantity or quality of effluent discharged from the POTW

questions.explanation: Adequate notice "shall include information on (i) the quality and quantity of effluent introduced into the POTW, and (ii) any anticipated impact of the change on the quantity or quality of effluent to be discharged from the POTW."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.42, Additional conditions applicable to specified categories of NPDES permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: adequate notice shall include information on (i) the quality and quantity of effluent introduced into the POTW, and (ii) any anticipated impact of the change on the quantity or quality of effluent to be discharged from the POTW.

questions.topic: Additional conditions for specified permit categories
questions.question: Under 122.42(a)(1), an existing manufacturing discharger must notify the Director of a routine or frequent discharge of a toxic pollutant not limited in its permit if the discharge will exceed which of the listed notification levels?

options.A: The highest of the listed notification levels
options.B: The lowest of the listed notification levels
options.C: The average of all the listed notification levels
options.D: Whichever listed level the discharger selects in its application

questions.explanation: The duty applies "if that discharge will exceed the highest of the following" notification levels.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.42, Additional conditions applicable to specified categories of NPDES permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: if that discharge will exceed the highest of the following

questions.question: Under 122.43(c), what must a permit give when a permit condition is incorporated by reference?

options.A: A full copy of the regulation attached as an appendix
options.B: A summary written by the permittee
options.C: A specific citation to the applicable regulations or requirements
options.D: The date the regulation was first proposed

questions.explanation: "All permit conditions shall be incorporated either expressly or by reference. If incorporated by reference, a specific citation to the applicable regulations or requirements must be given in the permit."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.43, Establishing permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: If incorporated by reference, a specific citation to the applicable regulations or requirements must be given in the permit.

questions.question: What does 122.44(a)(2)(ii) say about how long a monitoring waiver for a guideline-listed pollutant is good?

options.A: It is good for 10 years regardless of the permit term
options.B: It is good indefinitely once granted
options.C: It is good only for the term of the permit and is not available during the term of the first permit issued to a discharger
options.D: It is available only during the term of the first permit issued to a discharger

questions.explanation: "This waiver is good only for the term of the permit and is not available during the term of the first permit issued to a discharger."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.44, Establishing limitations, standards, and other permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: This waiver is good only for the term of the permit and is not available during the term of the first permit issued to a discharger.

questions.question: Under 122.44(g), which pollutants must the permit's list of pollutants subject to 24-hour reporting include?

options.A: Any toxic pollutant or hazardous substance, or any pollutant specifically identified as the method to control a toxic pollutant or hazardous substance
options.B: Only conventional pollutants such as BOD and TSS
options.C: Only pollutants that have no limit in the permit
options.D: Only pH and temperature

questions.explanation: "This list shall include any toxic pollutant or hazardous substance, or any pollutant specifically identified as the method to control a toxic pollutant or hazardous substance."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.44, Establishing limitations, standards, and other permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: This list shall include any toxic pollutant or hazardous substance, or any pollutant specifically identified as the method to control a toxic pollutant or hazardous substance.

questions.question: 122.44(i)(1)(iv)(A) gives two ways a method can be sufficiently sensitive. Which of these is one of them?

options.A: The method was published most recently
options.B: The method is the least costly approved method
options.C: The method minimum level (ML) is at least twice the effluent limit
options.D: The method minimum level (ML) is at or below the level of the effluent limit established in the permit for the measured pollutant

questions.explanation: A method is sufficiently sensitive when "The method minimum level (ML) is at or below the level of the effluent limit established in the permit for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter" or when "The method has the lowest ML of the analytical methods approved under 40 CFR part 136" or required under subchapter N or O.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.44, Establishing limitations, standards, and other permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The method minimum level (ML) is at or below the level of the effluent limit established in the permit for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter

questions.question: Except as provided in paragraphs (i)(4) and (5), what reporting frequency for monitoring results does 122.44(i)(2) set?

options.A: Monthly for every permittee
options.B: Case by case, dependent on the nature and effect of the discharge, but in no case less than once a year
options.C: Quarterly for POTWs and annually for all others
options.D: Once per permit term

questions.explanation: Reporting requirements "shall be established on a case-by-case basis with a frequency dependent on the nature and effect of the discharge, but in no case less than once a year."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.44, Establishing limitations, standards, and other permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall be established on a case-by-case basis with a frequency dependent on the nature and effect of the discharge, but in no case less than once a year.

questions.question: Under 122.48(b), the required monitoring that all permits specify, including type, intervals, and frequency, must be sufficient to yield what?

options.A: Data which are representative of the monitored activity, including continuous monitoring when appropriate
options.B: Data from the single day of highest flow each year
options.C: Data collected only during daylight hours
options.D: Data averaged over the full permit term

questions.explanation: Permits specify "Required monitoring including type, intervals, and frequency sufficient to yield data which are representative of the monitored activity including, when appropriate, continuous monitoring".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.48, Requirements for recording and reporting of monitoring results (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Required monitoring including type, intervals, and frequency sufficient to yield data which are representative of the monitored activity including, when appropriate, continuous monitoring

questions.question: Under 122.44(i)(1)(iv)(B), how is monitoring conducted for a pollutant that has no approved method under 40 CFR part 136 and no method otherwise required under subchapter N or O?

options.A: Monitoring is not required for that pollutant
options.B: The permittee chooses any laboratory method it prefers
options.C: Monitoring waits until EPA approves a method
options.D: According to a test procedure specified in the permit

questions.explanation: In that case, "monitoring shall be conducted according to a test procedure specified in the permit for such pollutants or pollutant parameters."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.44, Establishing limitations, standards, and other permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: monitoring shall be conducted according to a test procedure specified in the permit for such pollutants or pollutant parameters.

questions.topic: POTW pretreatment, BMPs and reissued permits
questions.question: Under 122.44(j)(2)(ii), when must a POTW provide a written technical evaluation of the need to revise local limits under 40 CFR 403.5(c)(1)?

options.A: Only when an industrial user asks for one
options.B: Following permit issuance or reissuance
options.C: With every discharge monitoring report
options.D: Only after a pass-through violation

questions.explanation: POTWs must "Provide a written technical evaluation of the need to revise local limits under 40 CFR 403.5(c)(1), following permit issuance or reissuance."

questions.topic: POTW pretreatment, BMPs and reissued permits
questions.question: Under 122.44(l)(1), except as provided in (l)(2) and absent materially and substantially changed circumstances, when a permit is renewed or reissued its interim effluent limitations must be at least as stringent as what?

options.A: The limits in the permittee's original application
options.B: The average effluent quality achieved during the last year
options.C: The final effluent limitations, standards, or conditions in the previous permit
options.D: The interim limits that applied in the first year of the previous permit

questions.explanation: When a permit is renewed or reissued, "interim effluent limitations, standards or conditions must be at least as stringent as the final effluent limitations, standards, or conditions in the previous permit".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.44, Establishing limitations, standards, and other permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: interim effluent limitations, standards or conditions must be at least as stringent as the final effluent limitations, standards, or conditions in the previous permit

questions.question: Under 122.45(d)(2), how are limitations for a POTW's continuous discharges stated, unless impracticable?

options.A: As instantaneous maximum and annual average limitations
options.B: As daily minimum and quarterly average limitations
options.C: As a single annual average limitation
options.D: As average weekly and average monthly discharge limitations

questions.explanation: For continuous discharges, limitations "shall unless impracticable be stated as" "Average weekly and average monthly discharge limitations for POTWs." Dischargers other than POTWs get maximum daily and average monthly limitations.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.45, Calculating NPDES permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Average weekly and average monthly discharge limitations for POTWs.

questions.question: Under 122.45(b)(1), what are a POTW's permit effluent limitations, standards, or prohibitions calculated on?

options.A: Design flow
options.B: A reasonable measure of actual production
options.C: Peak hourly flow on the day of sampling
options.D: The flow reported in the most recent DMR

questions.explanation: "In the case of POTWs, permit effluent limitations, standards, or prohibitions shall be calculated based on design flow."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.45, Calculating NPDES permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: In the case of POTWs, permit effluent limitations, standards, or prohibitions shall be calculated based on design flow.

questions.question: Under 122.45(c), unless one of its listed exceptions applies, in what terms must permit limitations for a metal be expressed?

options.A: The metal's concentration in the sewage sludge
options.B: Total recoverable metal as defined in 40 CFR part 136
options.C: Pounds of metal per ton of production
options.D: The metal's concentration in the receiving stream

questions.explanation: Limitations for a metal "shall be expressed in terms of “total recoverable metal” as defined in 40 CFR part 136 unless" one of the exceptions in (c)(1)–(3) applies.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.45, Calculating NPDES permit conditions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 122.45(f)(1) requires limits to be expressed in terms of mass except in listed cases. Which of these is named in the exception in 122.45(f)(1)(i)?

options.A: Biochemical oxygen demand
options.B: Zinc
options.C: Temperature
options.D: Ammonia

questions.explanation: Mass limits are required "except: (i) For pH, temperature, radiation, or other pollutants which cannot appropriately be expressed by mass".

questions.topic: Permit duration and schedules of compliance
questions.question: What does 122.46(c) allow the Director to do about a permit's term?

options.A: Issue any permit for a duration that is less than the full allowable term
options.B: Issue any permit for up to 10 years
options.C: Extend any permit indefinitely by letter
options.D: Let the permittee choose the permit's term

questions.explanation: "The Director may issue any permit for a duration that is less than the full allowable term under this section."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.46, Duration of permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The Director may issue any permit for a duration that is less than the full allowable term under this section.

questions.topic: Permit duration and schedules of compliance
questions.question: What deadline does 122.47(a)(4) set for the permittee to notify the Director in writing of compliance or noncompliance with an interim or final requirement of a schedule of compliance?

options.A: 24 hours after each interim date
options.B: 30 days after each interim date
options.C: With the next annual report
options.D: No later than 14 days following each interim date and the final date of compliance

questions.explanation: The permit must require that "no later than 14 days following each interim date and the final date of compliance, the permittee shall notify the Director in writing of its compliance or noncompliance".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.47, Schedules of compliance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: no later than 14 days following each interim date and the final date of compliance, the permittee shall notify the Director in writing of its compliance or noncompliance

questions.topic: Permit duration and schedules of compliance
questions.question: Except as provided in 122.47(b)(1)(ii), what must a schedule of compliance that exceeds 1 year from the date of permit issuance set forth?

options.A: Only the final compliance date
options.B: A bond to cover the cost of the work
options.C: Interim requirements and the dates for their achievement
options.D: A plan to stop discharging

questions.explanation: If the schedule "exceeds 1 year from the date of permit issuance, the schedule shall set forth interim requirements and the dates for their achievement."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.47, Schedules of compliance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: exceeds 1 year from the date of permit issuance, the schedule shall set forth interim requirements and the dates for their achievement.

questions.topic: Federal laws and disposal into wells, POTWs or land
questions.question: Under 122.50(a), when part of a discharger's process wastewater is disposed into a well, into a POTW, or by land application instead of to waters of the United States, how are the permit's effluent standards and limitations adjusted?

options.A: They are doubled to account for the other disposal
options.B: To reflect the reduced raw waste resulting from such disposal
options.C: They are dropped from the permit entirely
options.D: They stay unchanged in every case

questions.explanation: Applicable effluent standards and limitations "shall be adjusted to reflect the reduced raw waste resulting from such disposal."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.50, Disposal of pollutants into wells, into publicly owned treatment works or by land application (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall be adjusted to reflect the reduced raw waste resulting from such disposal.
